title: The Facebook–Cambridge Analytica Scandal Quiz
description: Test your understanding of data harvesting, API permissions, FTC regulations, and psychographic profiling.

questions.question: How was Cambridge Analytica able to harvest data from up to 87 million Facebook users when only ~270,000 took the quiz?
options: They breached Facebook's main servers using an SQL injection exploit
Facebook's v1.0 API permitted apps to harvest data from the installer's entire friend network without the friends' consent
They purchased the data directly from the dark web following a ransomware attack
They bribed Facebook database administrators to export internal customer tables
questions.explanation: Facebook's legacy Graph API allowed external applications to access profile data and 'likes' not only of the person who installed the app, but also of all their friends without their affirmative consent.

questions.question: What historic penalty did the US Federal Trade Commission (FTC) levy against Facebook in 2019 following the scandal?
options: A $500,000 regulatory citation
A $100 million corporate settlement
A historic $5 Billion civil penalty and corporate governance restructuring
A complete revocation of Facebook's operating license in North America
questions.explanation: The US FTC imposed an unprecedented $5 Billion penalty—the largest civil penalty in history for privacy violations—alongside mandatory independent oversight.

questions.question: What was the core violation under Section 5 of the FTC Act identified in the investigation?
options: Facebook sold pirated software
Facebook engaged in deceptive practices by violating its 2012 consent decree requiring explicit user consent before sharing data
Facebook failed to implement multi-factor authentication for user logins
Facebook engaged in insider trading of stock options
questions.explanation: The FTC alleged Facebook deceived users by misrepresenting the control users had over their personal data privacy settings and violating a prior 2012 FTC consent order.

questions.question: Under the UK Information Commissioner's Office (ICO) pre-GDPR investigation, why was Facebook fined only £500,000?
options: Because the ICO found no evidence of user harm in the United Kingdom
£500,000 was the maximum statutory cap permissible under the UK Data Protection Act 1998
Facebook agreed to settle the matter out of court with no admission of liability
The UK courts reduced the fine upon appeal
questions.explanation: Under the pre-GDPR Data Protection Act 1998, £500,000 was the absolute maximum legal fine the ICO could assess for data breaches, highlighting why GDPR's higher penalty ceiling was introduced.

questions.question: What is the most effective user precaution to prevent personal data exposure to third-party social apps?
options: Changing your profile password once every week
Regularly reviewing and revoking connected third-party app permissions in platform privacy settings
Posting a public status statement asserting copyright over your account data
Using social login across every website to consolidate accounts
questions.explanation: Regularly auditing authorized apps and removing access for dormant or unnecessary third-party services revokes API access tokens and prevents background data harvesting.

title: The Indian Bank Phishing & Smishing Campaigns Quiz
description: Assess your knowledge of KYC SMS phishing, OTP interception, IT Act Section 66D, and RBI customer liability rules.

questions.question: What primary psychological trigger is weaponized in 'Bank KYC suspension' smishing messages?
options: Curiosity about a lottery winning notification
Artificial urgency and fear of sudden financial account deactivation
Guilt regarding unpaid taxes
Desire to win an international cruise vacation
questions.explanation: Attackers manufacture artificial urgency by threatening that the victim's account or debit card will be blocked within 24 hours unless an immediate KYC update link is clicked.

questions.question: Which section of the Information Technology Act, 2000 specifically penalizes cheating by impersonation using a computer resource?
options: Section 65 (Tampering with computer source documents)
Section 66D (Punishment for cheating by personation by using computer resource)
Section 67 (Publishing obscene information)
Section 79 (Intermediary liability exemption)
questions.explanation: Section 66D of the IT Act, 2000 specifically punishes cheating by impersonating through a computer resource with imprisonment up to 3 years and a fine up to ₹1 Lakh.

questions.question: How do modern Adversary-in-the-Middle (AiTM) phishing sites defeat two-factor authentication OTPs?
options: They reverse-engineer the encryption keys on the user's SIM card
They capture credentials and OTPs entered by the victim in real-time and immediately forward them into the authentic banking session
They intercept the cellular tower signal using military radio jammers
They crack the user's password using automated brute-force dictionaries
questions.explanation: Reverse-proxy phishing kits relay the victim's inputs directly to the authentic banking website in real-time, grabbing session cookies and OTPs instantly.

questions.question: Under the RBI Customer Protection Directions, what is the customer's liability if an unauthorized fraud is reported within 3 working days?
options: Customer must pay 50% of the fraudulent amount
Customer is strictly liable for all financial damages
Zero customer liability applies for third-party breaches reported within 3 days
Customer liability is capped at ₹50,000 regardless of circumstances
questions.explanation: RBI guidelines mandate zero customer liability where unauthorized transactions occur due to bank negligence or third-party breaches where the customer notifies the bank within 3 working days.
questions.relatedTopic: RBI Master Direction on Customer Liability

questions.question: What is the official national helpline number for reporting financial cyber fraud in India?
questions.explanation: 1930 is India's dedicated national cyber fraud reporting helpline (formerly 155260) connected to the Citizen Financial Cyber Fraud Reporting System to freeze defrauded funds.

title: WannaCry Ransomware Attack Quiz
description: Evaluate your understanding of EternalBlue, SMBv1 vulnerabilities, UK NHS impact, and ransomware countermeasures.

questions.question: What specific exploit and protocol was weaponized by the WannaCry ransomware worm to spread across networks?
options: Log4Shell targeting Apache web servers
EternalBlue targeting unauthenticated SMBv1 buffer overflows (CVE-2017-0144)
Heartbleed targeting OpenSSL memory leaks
Dirty COW targeting the Linux kernel memory management
questions.explanation: WannaCry weaponized EternalBlue, an exploit targeting Microsoft's legacy SMBv1 protocol (CVE-2017-0144) leaked by the Shadow Brokers hacker group.

questions.question: How did security researcher Marcus Hutchins unintentionally halt the initial propagation of WannaCry?
options: By deploying a counter-virus that deleted the malware payload
By registering an unregistered hardcoded domain name found in the malware code, activating its kill switch
By hacking the attackers' Bitcoin command and control servers
By releasing a global Windows registry patch through Twitter
questions.explanation: The malware authors built in a check for an unregistered web domain. When Hutchins registered the domain for $10 to analyze it, the malware interpreted the live response as a sandbox check and halted execution.

questions.question: Under the UK Computer Misuse Act 1990, what maximum sentence can be applied for unauthorized acts causing serious damage to human welfare or critical services?
options: Up to 2 years imprisonment
Up to 10 years imprisonment
Up to life imprisonment (under Section 3ZA)
A fixed civil fine of £50,000
questions.explanation: Section 3ZA of the UK Computer Misuse Act provides up to life imprisonment for cyberattacks that cause serious damage to human welfare, the environment, state economy, or national security.

questions.question: Why was the UK National Health Service (NHS) particularly vulnerable to the WannaCry outbreak?
options: The NHS had disabled all network firewalls
Many NHS trusts were operating obsolete, unpatched Windows XP and Windows 7 systems and failed to apply the MS17-010 patch
An NHS employee intentionally downloaded the malware to protest hospital conditions
The NHS did not possess any computerized patient records
questions.explanation: The UK National Audit Office found the NHS was heavily dependent on legacy Windows systems, had fragmented IT governance, and had failed to deploy Microsoft's MS17-010 patch released two months prior.

questions.question: What is the recommended 3-2-1 backup strategy for protecting data against ransomware extortion?
options: 3 copies of data, on 2 different media types, with 1 copy kept offline or offsite
3 cloud providers, 2 passwords, 1 admin account
3 backups per day, 2 per week, 1 per month
3 hard drives stored in 2 desks on 1 floor
questions.explanation: The industry standard 3-2-1 rule dictates maintaining 3 total copies of data, across 2 different storage media types, with at least 1 copy kept completely immutable and disconnected (offline) from the network.

title: The Instagram Data Scraping & Exposure Quiz
description: Test your knowledge of automated API scraping, GDPR Data Protection by Design, and teen privacy protections.

questions.question: What architectural setting in Instagram led to the exposure of contact details of millions of teenage users?
options: A zero-day SQL injection in the login authentication module
Default settings on business accounts that publicly exposed contact phone numbers and emails in the web page source without age restrictions
A malicious firmware update pushed to iPhone and Android cameras
A rogue insider selling private direct messages on Telegram
questions.explanation: When teenage users converted accounts to business profiles to access view metrics, Instagram defaulted their email addresses and phone numbers to publicly queryable fields without age verification.

questions.question: What landmark GDPR penalty was imposed by the Irish Data Protection Commission (DPC) regarding Instagram's handling of children's data?
options: €10 Million
€100 Million
€405 Million
€1.2 Billion
questions.explanation: In September 2022, the Irish DPC issued a massive €405 Million fine against Meta following an inquiry into children's data privacy violations under GDPR Articles 5, 12, 24, and 25.

questions.question: What key principle under GDPR Article 25 was violated by defaulting teen accounts to public contact visibility?
options: Right to be Forgotten
Data Protection by Design and by Default
Cross-Border Data Transfer Equality
Decoupled Algorithmic Processing
questions.explanation: Article 25 mandates 'Data Protection by Design and by Default', requiring companies to build default settings that prioritize user privacy without requiring manual user hardening.

questions.question: How does India's Digital Personal Data Protection Act, 2023 specifically protect children under Section 9?
options: It bans all children from using mobile phones
It prohibits behavioral monitoring, tracking, and targeted advertisements directed at minors without parental consent
It forces children to use only government-operated social media platforms
It requires schools to confiscate digital devices during exams
questions.explanation: Section 9 of the DPDP Act 2023 strictly prohibits data fiduciaries from undertaking tracking, behavioral monitoring, or targeted advertising directed at children under 18.

questions.question: What is an effective defensive measure platforms can implement to prevent mass automated API scraping?
options: Requiring all users to submit notarized identity documents
Implementing IP rate limiting, bot behavior analysis, and requiring authentication for sensitive profile endpoints
Deleting all public user profile directories from search engines
Limiting internet access to daytime hours
questions.explanation: Rate limiting, automated bot fingerprinting, CAPTCHAs, and eliminating unauthenticated bulk API endpoints are standard techniques to mitigate automated web scraping.

title: Celebrity Deepfake Scams & AI Voice Clones Quiz
description: Evaluate your understanding of synthetic media, IT Rules 2021 intermediary obligations, and AI impersonation legalities.

questions.question: What machine learning technology primarily drives the generation of realistic face-swap deepfakes?
options: Linear regression modeling
Generative Adversarial Networks (GANs) and latent diffusion models
Rule-based expert systems
Optical Character Recognition (OCR) pipelines
questions.explanation: Generative Adversarial Networks (GANs) and modern diffusion architectures use competing generator and discriminator neural networks to synthesize hyper-realistic synthetic video and audio.

questions.question: Under Rule 3(2)(b) of the Information Technology (Intermediary Guidelines and Digital Media Ethics Code) Rules, 2021, what is the mandatory takedown timeline for non-consensual sexually explicit or morphed content?
options: Within 24 hours of receipt of complaint
Within 7 working days
Within 30 calendar days
Only after a formal high court judgment is delivered
questions.explanation: Rule 3(2)(b) of IT Rules 2021 obligates intermediaries to take down or disable access to non-consensual morphed, impersonating, or sexually explicit content within 24 hours of notification.

questions.question: Which Indian legal doctrine protects public figures from unauthorized commercial exploitation of their voice and likeness?
options: Doctrine of Sovereign Immunity
Common Law Personality Rights and the Tort of Passing Off
Patent Exclusivity Clause
Eminent Domain Doctrine
questions.explanation: Indian High Courts have repeatedly affirmed Personality Rights and the tort of passing off to prevent unauthorized commercial exploitation, synthetic imitation, and false endorsement of celebrities' personas.

questions.question: What forensic visual cue can frequently help identify a generative synthetic video (deepfake)?
options: The video is recorded in black and white
Unnatural eye-blinking rates, irregular teeth alignment, warping around jaw boundaries, and desynchronized audio cadence
The video automatically closes after 30 seconds
The presence of a mandatory government digital stamp
questions.explanation: Synthetic generation models often struggle with complex temporal consistency, creating artifacts like abnormal blinking, ear/jawline blurring, unnatural lighting reflections, and subtle lip-sync lags.

questions.question: What emerging technical standard enables content publishers to cryptographically certify the authentic origin and edit history of digital media?
options: OAuth 2.0 Client Tokens
C2PA (Coalition for Content Provenance and Authenticity) Content Credentials
SSL Certificate Pinning
DNSSEC Host Mapping
questions.explanation: The C2PA standard embeds cryptographically signed metadata ('Content Credentials') into images and videos, documenting origin, creation device, and modifications.

title: Online Harassment, Doxxing & Cyberstalking Quiz
description: Test your comprehension of digital harassment laws, IPC Section 354D / BNS Section 78, and evidence preservation.

questions.question: What constitutes the cybercrime of 'doxxing'?
options: Overwhelming a web server with artificial HTTP traffic
Maliciously publishing a person's private personal information (home address, phone number, workplace) online to incite harassment
Cracking a user's Wi-Fi network password using a dictionary attack
Filing a patent on public domain software source code
questions.explanation: Doxxing refers to the unauthorized publication of private identifying information online with the intent to subject the victim to harassment, real-world danger, or intimidation.

questions.question: Under Section 354D of the Indian Penal Code (now Section 78 of Bharatiya Nyaya Sanhita), what specific digital conduct is explicitly criminalized?
options: Using an ad-blocker on commercial websites
Monitoring by a man of the internet, email, or electronic communication used by a woman without legitimate reason
Forwarding encrypted emails without a digital signature
Downloading open-source operating system ISO images
questions.explanation: Section 354D IPC explicitly defines stalking to include monitoring a woman's internet use, electronic communications, or digital social media presence.

questions.question: Which section of the Information Technology Act, 2000 punishes the intentional capture, transmission, or publication of images of a person's private areas without consent?
options: Section 43A
Section 66E (Punishment for violation of privacy)
Section 72A
Section 69B
questions.explanation: Section 66E of the IT Act penalizes intentionally capturing, publishing, or transmitting images of private body parts without consent with imprisonment up to 3 years and/or fine up to ₹2 Lakh.

questions.question: When experiencing persistent cyberstalking, why is taking immediate timestamped screenshots of messages and profile URLs critical?
options: Because courts only accept paper photographs developed in darkrooms
Because electronic evidence can be swiftly edited, deleted, or accounts deactivated by the perpetrator before police can issue subpoenas
Because screenshots automatically block the perpetrator's IP address
Because social media companies charge fees to retrieve deleted chats
questions.explanation: Digital evidence is highly ephemeral. Capturing timestamped screenshots, unique account handles, and message headers before content is deleted preserves vital evidence for cybercrime complaints.

questions.question: On India's National Cyber Crime Reporting Portal (cybercrime.gov.in), what specialized provision exists for victims of cyber harassment involving women or children?
options: The ability to file complaints anonymously to initiate urgent takedown of sensitive or explicit content
A mandatory ₹5,000 filing fee
A requirement to appear in court in New Delhi within 48 hours
Automatic public publishing of the suspect's tax records
questions.explanation: The portal provides a specialized 'Report Crime Against Women/Child' channel that permits confidential and anonymous reporting to swiftly remove non-consensual explicit material.

title: State-Sponsored Cyber Espionage: SolarWinds Supply Chain Quiz
description: Assess your understanding of software supply chain compromises, SUNBURST backdoor mechanics, and CISA directives.

questions.question: How did the threat actors in the SolarWinds breach successfully deliver malicious backdoors to 18,000 enterprise customers?
options: By sending 18,000 individual phishing emails to system administrators
By compromising SolarWinds' software build pipeline and injecting malicious code (SUNBURST) into officially signed software updates
By exploiting a zero-day vulnerability in home Wi-Fi routers
By physically planting compromised USB drives in customer parking lots
questions.explanation: Attackers executed a sophisticated software supply chain attack by poisoning the build pipeline, inserting the SUNBURST backdoor into valid, digitally signed Orion software updates.

questions.question: Why was the malicious SUNBURST code not immediately detected by antivirus software on customer systems?
options: Because all customer antivirus software was turned off
Because the malicious DLL was digitally signed with SolarWinds' authentic corporate cryptographic certificate and lay dormant for two weeks
Because the code was written in ancient assembly language
Because the malware deleted the operating system logs upon installation
questions.explanation: Because the malicious dynamic-link library (DLL) carried a valid digital signature from SolarWinds and remained completely dormant for up to two weeks before beaconing, endpoint security tools trusted it.

questions.question: What emergency legal power did CISA exercise in response to the SolarWinds breach on December 13, 2020?
options: Declaring nationwide martial law
Issuing Emergency Directive 21-01 requiring federal civilian agencies to immediately disconnect Orion servers
Shutting down the civilian transatlantic subsea internet cables
Nationalizing private software development companies
questions.explanation: Under statutory authority of the Cybersecurity Information Sharing Act, CISA issued Emergency Directive 21-01 compelling all federal civilian agencies to disconnect Orion servers immediately.

questions.question: What key requirement did US Presidential Executive Order 14028 mandate for federal software procurement post-SolarWinds?
options: All software must be open-source and free of cost
Suppliers must provide a Software Bill of Materials (SBOM) and demonstrate secure, isolated software development environments
No foreign citizens can be employed as software engineers
Federal agencies must discontinue the use of all computer networks
questions.explanation: Executive Order 14028 mandated Software Bills of Materials (SBOM), multi-factor authentication, and strict secure software development standards for all government software vendors.

questions.question: In enterprise cybersecurity, what architectural philosophy prevents an adversary from moving laterally across internal networks after an initial compromise?
options: Perimeter-only defense with trusted internal zones
Zero Trust Architecture (never trust, always verify, least privilege, micro-segmentation)
Storing all company passwords in a shared spreadsheet
Disabling operating system firewall notifications
questions.explanation: Zero Trust Architecture enforces continuous authentication, micro-segmentation, and least privilege, ensuring that even if one server is compromised, lateral traversal is halted.

title: UPI Payment Fraud & QR Code Phishing Waves Quiz
description: Evaluate your understanding of UPI payment protocols, QR code mechanics, IT Act 66D, and financial fraud hotlines.

questions.question: What is the universal architectural rule regarding the Unified Payments Interface (UPI) PIN?
options: A UPI PIN is needed to both receive and send payments
A UPI PIN is ONLY required to DEBIT (send) money, NEVER to receive money
A UPI PIN is required whenever an SMS notification is received
Entering a UPI PIN verifies that your identity is clean from criminal records
questions.explanation: Entering a UPI PIN authorizes the immediate debiting of funds from your linked bank account. You NEVER need to enter your PIN or scan a QR code to receive money.

questions.question: How do scammers on platforms like OLX manipulate victims using UPI 'Collect Requests'?
options: They hack into the victim's phone hardware through the charging cable
They send a Collect Request disguised as a payment receipt and urge the victim to approve and enter their PIN to 'claim' the advance payment
They cancel the user's internet banking subscription
They install a physical card skimmer inside the phone screen
questions.explanation: Fraudsters initiate a reverse 'Collect Request' (which pulls money from the victim), falsely telling the seller: 'Approve this request and enter your PIN so the advance gets credited.'

questions.question: Under the Information Technology Act, 2000, which sections are primarily registered in police FIRs for UPI payment fraud?
options: Section 66C (Identity Theft) and Section 66D (Cheating by Impersonation)
Section 69A and Section 79
Section 292 and Section 294
Section 120B exclusively
questions.explanation: Sections 66C (fraudulent use of electronic passwords/PINs) and 66D (cheating by personation using a computer resource) are the primary IT Act provisions invoked for UPI fraud.
questions.relatedTopic: IT Act Provisions for UPI Fraud

questions.question: What is the 'Golden Window' period for reporting a financial cyber fraud to Helpline 1930 for the highest probability of recovering funds?
options: Within 1 to 2 hours of the fraudulent debit
After waiting 30 days for a bank statement
Within 6 months of filing a physical tax return
Reporting time does not affect fund recovery at all
questions.explanation: Reporting within the first 1 to 2 hours ('Golden Window') allows the Indian Cyber Crime Coordination Centre (I4C) system to freeze the funds before money mules withdraw them at ATMs.

questions.question: When scanning a merchant QR code in a store, what safety check should you perform before entering your PIN?
options: Ensure your screen brightness is at 100%
Verify the beneficiary's registered business name displayed on the payment screen matches the physical store
Restart your phone twice before confirming the payment
Ask the cashier to provide their personal home address
questions.explanation: Always check the verified merchant name displayed on the payment confirmation screen before entering your PIN to avoid paying malicious QR codes pasted over legitimate stickers.

title: Target Corporation Supply Chain & POS Data Breach Quiz
description: Assess your knowledge of POS RAM scraping malware, third-party vendor risk, and PCI DSS compliance.

questions.question: How did cybercriminals initially gain access to Target Corporation's corporate network in 2013?
options: By guessing the root password on Target's public website
By stealing vendor portal credentials from an external third-party HVAC contractor through a phishing email
By bribing in-store cashiers to hand over register flash drives
By exploiting a flaw in Target's mobile consumer shopping app
questions.explanation: Attackers phished employees at Fazio Mechanical Services, a refrigeration contractor, stealing vendor credentials that had unsegmented routing into Target's wider corporate network.

questions.question: What type of malware was deployed on Target's cash registers to steal 40 million credit card records?
options: A crypto-ransomware worm
A RAM-scraping (memory-scraping) trojan ('BlackPOS') that intercepted card data in volatile memory before encryption
A distributed denial of service botnet
An email auto-responder script
questions.explanation: BlackPOS scraped track 1 and 2 credit card data directly from the Point of Sale register's volatile RAM during the brief millisecond window when the card was swiped before encryption occurred.

questions.question: What network architecture failure allowed attackers to move from a facilities vendor portal to checkout registers?
options: Lack of high-speed fiber internet connections
Inadequate network segmentation between supplier portals and the Cardholder Data Environment (CDE)
Target was using satellite internet instead of cables
All cash registers were connected to public customer Wi-Fi
questions.explanation: Target failed to enforce strict micro-segmentation, allowing traffic to route laterally from general vendor billing zones directly into the sensitive PCI cardholder transaction environment.

questions.question: Under the FTC Act Section 5, why did the multi-state attorneys general investigation hold Target liable?
options: Because Target failed to employ reasonable and appropriate data security safeguards to protect customer data
Because Target failed to open its stores on time on Black Friday
Because Target charged excessive credit card processing fees
Because Target refused to accept cash payments
questions.explanation: State Attorneys General and federal regulators held that failing to maintain reasonable vendor access controls and ignoring intrusion alerts constituted unfair commercial security practices.

questions.question: What major payment hardware technology was widely accelerated across the United States as a direct consequence of the Target breach?
options: Magnetic stripe card swiping
EMV chip cards and Point-to-Point Encryption (P2PE)
Paper check processing machines
Cryptocurrency barcode scanning
questions.explanation: The Target breach catalyzed the US migration from easily cloned magnetic stripes to cryptographic EMV chip cards and Point-to-Point Encryption (P2PE).

title: LinkedIn Credential Theft & Mass Profile Scraping Quiz
description: Evaluate your understanding of public web scraping, API enumeration, CFAA jurisprudence, and hiQ Labs v. LinkedIn.

questions.question: In the landmark case hiQ Labs, Inc. v. LinkedIn Corp., what did the US Ninth Circuit Court of Appeals determine regarding automated scraping?
options: Scraping public data is punishable by mandatory 10-year prison sentences under CFAA
Querying publicly accessible internet pages that require no login or authentication does not constitute access 'without authorization' under the CFAA
All web scrapers must register with the Federal Communications Commission
Websites are legally forbidden from implementing rate-limiting
questions.explanation: The Ninth Circuit held that the Computer Fraud and Abuse Act (CFAA) anti-hacking provisions were intended to prevent breaking into gated systems, not viewing or querying publicly open web data.

questions.question: How did attackers harvest records of approximately 700 million LinkedIn users in 2021?
options: They breached LinkedIn's internal oracle database via zero-day SQL injection
They automated requests against official APIs and public profile endpoints using sequential user IDs (parameter tampering/enumeration)
They stole physical hard drives from LinkedIn's primary data center
They spoofed LinkedIn's top-level DNS domain name
questions.explanation: Attackers did not compromise core internal servers; rather, they used automated bots to systematically cycle through user IDs on open APIs and public profiles, scraping exposed attributes at scale.

questions.question: Under the European Union GDPR, why can commercial entities still face heavy fines for scraping 'publicly available' personal data?
options: Because European law requires all internet bots to pay royalties to creators
Because personal data remains protected by GDPR principles (purpose limitation and legal basis) regardless of whether it is publicly displayed
Because GDPR bans all forms of search engines in Europe
Because scraping uses electrical power regulated by EU green energy laws
questions.explanation: Under GDPR, the fact that personal information is publicly accessible on the web does NOT grant third parties a lawful basis to scrape, aggregate, and commercialize it without user consent.

questions.question: What technical defense is most effective at preventing automated bots from enumerating and dumping millions of user profiles?
options: Changing the color of the website header daily
Behavioral rate limiting, IP reputation filtering, CAPTCHAs, and requiring authentication to access profile contact fields
Encrypting HTML tags with AES-256
Disabling CSS stylesheets on the server
questions.explanation: Throttling request velocity via rate limiting, detecting headless browser signatures, deploying CAPTCHAs, and requiring session authentication mitigate automated mass scraping.

questions.question: What privacy setting should individuals configure on professional networking platforms to reduce their exposure to data scrapers?
options: Make sure your personal phone number and personal email are hidden from public web search engines and non-connections
Use your password as your public username
Connect with every single anonymous invitation you receive
Never log into your account from a desktop computer
questions.explanation: Restricting the visibility of sensitive contact fields (phone number, private email) to approved direct connections prevents automated scrapers from weaponizing your dossier.

title: Cosmos Bank Pune Malware & ATM Switch Bypass Quiz
description: Test your understanding of ATM switch server hijacking, SWIFT fraud, IT Act Section 43/66, and banking security resilience.

questions.question: How did attackers succeed in withdrawing ₹78 Crore from ATMs worldwide during the Cosmos Bank heist without actual account balances?
options: They physically blew up ATM cash boxes with explosives in Pune
They installed a rogue proxy switch server that intercepted authorization requests and returned forged approval codes to ATMs
They hacked every single ATM machine's firmware with a hardware thumb drive
They altered the bank's printed account ledger books by hand
questions.explanation: Attackers inserted a rogue switch server between the bank's core banking system and the payment gateway, forging approval responses ('Code 00') for cloned card withdrawals at ATMs globally.

questions.question: Besides the ATM cash-outs, what other banking channel was compromised to steal an additional ₹13.9 Crore?
options: UPI QR code collect requests
Forged SWIFT financial messaging instructions to a bank in Hong Kong
Counterfeit paper bearer checks presented at branch tellers
Cryptocurrency smart contract drains
questions.explanation: Attackers generated 3 unauthorized SWIFT MT103 financial messages, transferring ₹13.9 Crore directly to an account at Hang Seng Bank in Hong Kong.

questions.question: Under the Information Technology Act, 2000, which section specifically addresses damage, extraction, or destruction of computer systems and data?
options: Section 43 (Penalty and compensation for damage to computer system)
Section 79 (Exemption from liability of intermediary in certain cases)
Section 65 (Tampering with computer source documents only)
Section 81 (Act to have overriding effect)
questions.explanation: Section 43 provides penalties and civil liability for unauthorized access, downloading, damage, disruption, or denial of access to any computer or computer network.

questions.question: What baseline security measure mandated by RBI's Cyber Security Framework would have helped alert bank operators during the initial intrusion?
options: Continuous 24/7 Security Operations Center (SOC) monitoring and behavioral anomaly detection
Installing antivirus on employee home computers only
Sending paper letters to account holders whenever an ATM is used
Shutting down the internet connection every night
questions.explanation: A proactive 24/7 SOC with real-time SIEM correlation detects unusual connection attempts, proxy redirection of core switches, and high-velocity international ATM spikes.
questions.relatedTopic: RBI Cyber Security Framework for Banks

questions.question: What architectural defense prevents a compromised card switch from settling fraudulent transactions?
options: Allowing cards to be used without PINs
Real-time dual-channel cryptographic reconciliation between Core Banking (CBS) logs and Payment Switch ledgers
Printing transaction receipts in triplicate
Disabling ATM withdrawals on weekends
questions.explanation: Independent cryptographic cross-verification ensures that a payment gateway cannot debit settlement accounts without authenticated ledger verification from the core banking host.

title: Equifax Credit Bureau Apache Struts Breach Quiz
description: Evaluate your knowledge of open-source vulnerabilities (CVE-2017-5638), asset inventory controls, and FTC enforcement orders.

questions.question: What specific software vulnerability did attackers exploit to breach Equifax's online dispute portal?
options: A weak default administrator password on the root database
CVE-2017-5638, a remote code execution vulnerability in the Apache Struts web framework
A zero-day hardware flaw in Intel processor chips
An unencrypted Bluetooth connection between office printers
questions.explanation: The breach exploited CVE-2017-5638 in Apache Struts, which allowed attackers to execute remote system commands via crafted Content-Type HTTP headers.

questions.question: Why was Equifax's internal security team unable to detect the exfiltration of 147 million records for over two months?
options: The hackers turned off the power to the entire data center
An internal SSL inspection certificate on network monitoring devices had expired 19 months prior, leaving traffic analysis blind
Equifax had no internet connection installed
The attackers erased the backup tapes by hand
questions.explanation: Equifax's intrusion detection system failed to inspect encrypted traffic because an internal SSL certificate had expired 19 months earlier; once IT renewed it, the breach was discovered immediately.

questions.question: What was the total monetary scope of the global settlement Equifax reached with the FTC, CFPB, and 50 states?
options: Up to $700 Million in consumer restitution, relief, and civil penalties
$5 Million in legal fees
$100 Million fine with no customer restitution
No financial penalty was assessed due to lack of proof
questions.explanation: Equifax agreed to pay up to $700 Million to resolve federal and state investigations, funding free credit monitoring and direct restitution for affected consumers.

questions.question: What foundational IT governance failure prevented Equifax from patching the Struts vulnerability when US-CERT warned about it?
options: They did not have any software developers on staff
They lacked an accurate asset and software inventory identifying which web servers were running Apache Struts
Microsoft refused to support their operating systems
Apache charges $1 Million per security patch
questions.explanation: Congressional investigations revealed Equifax lacked a centralized software inventory, meaning security teams did not know which external-facing servers actually ran vulnerable Apache Struts code.

questions.question: What protective step should consumers take if their Social Security Number or national ID is exposed in a credit bureau breach?
options: Place a free credit freeze on their credit files with all major bureaus to block unauthorized loans
Close all existing bank accounts and stop paying taxes
Throw away their physical driver's license card
Delete their email address and disconnect their home Wi-Fi
questions.explanation: Placing a credit freeze prevents credit reporting agencies from releasing your credit report without authorization, preventing fraudsters from opening loans in your name.

title: Twitter VIP Account Takeover & Bitcoin Scam Quiz
description: Assess your understanding of voice phishing (vishing), admin tool segregation, and CFAA computer fraud statutes.

questions.question: What social engineering technique did the teenage hackers use to obtain internal credentials from Twitter employees in 2020?
options: Sending malware through Slack file attachments
Voice phishing (vishing) phone calls pretending to be internal IT helpdesk staff assisting with remote-work VPN issues
Bribing Twitter data center security guards to enter the server room
Guessing employee birthday passwords on public login pages
questions.explanation: The attackers called remote-working customer service employees, impersonated Twitter's corporate IT department, and directed them to a spoofed VPN portal that harvested credentials and 2FA tokens.

questions.question: What internal capability allowed the attackers to take over 45 high-profile accounts (including Obama, Musk, and Gates)?
options: Access to Twitter's proprietary internal administrative customer-support tool that could change registered email addresses
A cryptographic flaw in Twitter's password hashing algorithm
Direct control of physical cellular cell towers in San Francisco
A vulnerability in Apple iOS operating systems
questions.explanation: The attackers gained access to an internal customer-support admin tool that possessed unrestricted 'god-mode' capabilities to reset account emails and disable multi-factor protections.

questions.question: Under the Computer Fraud and Abuse Act (18 U.S.C. § 1030), what crime was charged against the perpetrators for extorting Bitcoin?
options: Copyright infringement of software manuals
Conspiracy to commit wire fraud and intentional unauthorized access to a protected computer to perpetrate fraud
Maritime piracy on digital networks
Violation of federal securities registration laws
questions.explanation: The US Department of Justice and Florida state prosecutors charged the hackers with wire fraud, computer fraud under 18 U.S.C. § 1030, and organized fraudulent communication.

questions.question: What governance control would have prevented a single compromised employee account from resetting VIP Twitter handles?
options: Sending an automated email to the user
Dual-control / 'Four-Eyes' authorization requiring independent verification from a second senior administrator
Allowing only employees with computer science degrees to use computers
Requiring all employees to work exclusively from physical headquarters
questions.explanation: The 'Four-Eyes' principle (dual authorization) mandates that sensitive, high-risk administrative operations require mutual approval by two authorized staff members before execution.

questions.question: Why are physical FIDO2 hardware security keys (e.g., YubiKeys) immune to voice phishing and reverse-proxy credential harvesting?
options: They have built-in biometric face scanners
They cryptographically bind authentication tokens to the authentic browser origin URL, refusing to authenticate on spoofed phishing domains
They disable internet access on the computer during login
They do not require any user interaction
questions.explanation: FIDO2 WebAuthn keys bind cryptographic challenges to the exact TLS origin in the browser address bar. If a user is on a phishing site, the domain mismatch prevents token disclosure.

title: Colonial Pipeline Ransomware & Critical Infrastructure Quiz
description: Evaluate your knowledge of OT/IT convergence risks, legacy VPN entry points, CIRCIA reporting, and DarkSide ransomware.

questions.question: What was the initial point of compromise that allowed the DarkSide ransomware group into Colonial Pipeline's corporate network?
options: A compromised supply chain update to the pipeline physical control valves
A single compromised password for an inactive, legacy VPN account that lacked multi-factor authentication (MFA)
An infected USB drive found in a parking lot
A physical break-in at a pipeline pumping station in New Jersey
questions.explanation: Attackers discovered a leaked password for a legacy virtual private network (VPN) account that was dormant but still active and did not have multi-factor authentication enabled.

questions.question: Why did Colonial Pipeline shut down its physical pipeline operations if the ransomware only infected the corporate IT network?
options: Because the physical pipeline pipes had exploded
Because the billing and accounting systems were encrypted, making it impossible to meter and bill customers for delivered fuel
Because the federal government ordered an immediate military evacuation of all pipelines
Because the pipeline was out of crude oil supply
questions.explanation: While operational technology (OT) pumping systems were uninfected, Colonial could not bill commercial customers or track fuel volumes due to the loss of corporate IT billing software.

questions.question: How did the FBI successfully recover 63.7 of the 75 Bitcoin paid by Colonial Pipeline to the extortionists?
options: By hacking the Bitcoin blockchain consensus network and rewriting the ledger
By obtaining the private cryptographic key to the criminal syndicate's cryptocurrency wallet address
By asking the Russian government to wire the money back
By suing the cryptocurrency mining pools in court
questions.explanation: The FBI tracked the ransom payments through the public blockchain and seized the funds after acquiring the private cryptographic keys for the specific digital wallet holding the extortion proceeds.

questions.question: What historic federal legislation was enacted by the US Congress in 2022 directly following the Colonial Pipeline incident?
options: The Computer Fraud and Abuse Act Amendment
The Cyber Incident Reporting for Critical Infrastructure Act (CIRCIA)
The Patriot Act Extension
The National Data Privacy and Shield Act
questions.explanation: CIRCIA mandates that critical infrastructure operators report substantial cyber incidents to CISA within 72 hours and any ransomware extortion payments within 24 hours.

questions.question: What architectural principle ensures that operational infrastructure can continue pumping safely during a corporate IT outage?
options: Full cloud migration of all industrial motors
Architectural decoupling of OT and IT networks with offline manual operation capability
Sharing domain admin accounts between office laptops and factory controllers
Connecting all pipeline pressure valves to the corporate email server
questions.explanation: Air-gapping or strictly segmenting OT industrial control systems from business IT, combined with validated manual override procedures, ensures essential service continuity.

title: AIIMS Delhi Healthcare Ransomware Incident Quiz
description: Test your comprehension of healthcare infrastructure cyber threats, IT Act Section 66F cyber terrorism, and CERT-In directions.

questions.question: What critical hospital systems were paralyzed during the November 2022 ransomware attack on AIIMS New Delhi?
options: Physical operating room surgical lights
Centralized e-Hospital servers managing outpatient registrations, lab report generation, patient admissions, and billing
Ambulance engine braking controls
Hospital cafeteria automated vending machines
questions.explanation: The ransomware encrypted database servers hosted by the National Informatics Centre (NIC), knocking out electronic health records, lab reports, digital billing, and OPD registrations.

questions.question: Which severe penal provision of the Information Technology Act, 2000 was invoked in the police FIR registered for the AIIMS attack?
options: Section 43A (Corporate compensation)
Section 66F (Punishment for Cyber Terrorism)
Section 67 (Obscenity)
Section 72 (Breach of confidentiality)
questions.explanation: Delhi Police IFSO registered the case under Section 66F (Cyber Terrorism), which carries up to life imprisonment for acts intentionally disrupting critical infrastructure or state health delivery.

questions.question: Under the CERT-In Cyber Security Directions issued in April 2022, within what mandatory timeframe must organizations report cybersecurity incidents?
options: Within 6 hours of noticing the incident
Within 30 calendar days
Within 1 year of forensic conclusion
Reporting is entirely voluntary under Indian law
questions.explanation: The CERT-In Directions issued under Section 70B(6) of the IT Act mandate that all service providers, intermediaries, data centers, and government entities report cyber incidents within 6 hours.

questions.question: How did AIIMS clinical staff maintain patient care throughout the two-week digital blackout?
options: They sent all 12,000 daily patients to private clinics
They instituted emergency manual protocols, using paper registers, physical charts, and hand-carried lab slips
They paid the attackers' ransom within 24 hours to restore the servers
They stopped admitting all emergency trauma cases
questions.explanation: Hospital administration deployed hundreds of additional staff to run a completely manual paper-based workflow for registration, triage, and hand-delivered laboratory results.

questions.question: What architectural flaw in university and hospital campus networks frequently exposes healthcare servers to malware?
options: Using fiber optic cables
Inadequate network segmentation between academic/research Wi-Fi, administrative PCs, and core clinical databases
Using Linux operating systems instead of Windows
Having too many physical emergency exits in the building
questions.explanation: Failing to segment general student/faculty campus networks from critical clinical databases allows malware from an unpatched student workstation to move laterally into vital hospital systems.

title: Mass Google OAuth Worm & Account Phishing Quiz
description: Evaluate your understanding of consent phishing, OAuth 2.0 token grants, API scopes, and authorization safeguards.

questions.question: How did the May 2017 'Google Docs' phishing campaign bypass traditional password theft and multi-factor authentication?
options: By guessing passwords using quantum computers
By tricking users into granting legitimate OAuth 2.0 access tokens to a rogue third-party app deceptively named 'Google Docs'
By spoofing Google's global satellite uplink stations
By sending infected USB keys through postal mail
questions.explanation: The attack used 'consent phishing'. Users authenticated legitimately on real Google servers, but authorized a malicious third-party app named 'Google Docs' that was granted API tokens to read emails and contacts.

questions.question: How did the rogue application spread automatically across millions of inboxes in under an hour?
options: It exploited a kernel zero-day on Android phones
Once granted mailbox permissions, it programmatically read the victim's contact book and emailed the same phishing invitation to all contacts via the Google API
It bought advertising space on Google Search results
It hacked internet service provider routers
questions.explanation: Because the rogue app had legitimate programmatic API access to the victim's contacts and mailbox, it functioned as an automated worm, blasting invitations to all contacts immediately.

questions.question: What major platform security policy did Google implement in response to the rogue OAuth campaign?
options: Discontinuing all third-party integrations with Google services
Requiring mandatory developer verification, domain audits, and explicit warning screens for unverified apps requesting sensitive scopes
Banning all Google Docs sharing links
Making all Google accounts paid subscriptions
questions.explanation: Google overhauled its OAuth verification process, requiring strict multi-stage security verification and brand validation before apps can request access to sensitive Gmail or Drive scopes.

questions.question: When reviewing an OAuth consent prompt, what detail reveals the true identity of the requesting application?
options: The font size used for the title
Clicking on the developer or app name to inspect the registered developer email address and actual web domain
The color of the 'Allow' button
The time of day the prompt appears
questions.explanation: Clicking the app name in legitimate OAuth consent dialogs reveals developer metadata, domain ownership, and whether Google has independently verified the developer.

questions.question: What administrative control can enterprise IT administrators enforce to protect corporate Google Workspace domains from illicit OAuth apps?
options: Enforce OAuth app whitelisting to block non-approved third-party apps from accessing corporate data
Disable all employee monitor screens at 5 PM
Prohibit employees from sending emails outside the company
Change the company website domain weekly
questions.explanation: Workspace administrators can configure App Access Controls to restrict third-party API access exclusively to trusted, admin-approved applications, neutralizing rogue consent grants.

title: SIM Swap OTP Interception & Account Takeover Quiz
description: Assess your knowledge of mobile identity theft, SMS 2FA vulnerabilities, DoT cooling regulations, and account hardening.

questions.question: How do cybercriminals execute a fraudulent SIM swap attack?
options: By cloning the victim's phone screen using Bluetooth sniffing
By impersonating the victim using fake or stolen ID documents at telecom stores or helpdesks to transfer the phone number to an attacker-controlled SIM card
By hacking into cellular satellites orbiting the earth
By purchasing physical SIM cards in bulk from online retailers
questions.explanation: Perpetrators use stolen demographic info (Aadhaar, PAN, billing details) to deceive customer care staff into reissuing the victim's mobile number onto a new blank SIM card.

questions.question: What is the immediate symptom experienced by a victim when an unauthorized SIM swap occurs on their phone?
options: The phone battery percentage jumps to 100%
The phone abruptly loses all cellular network connectivity ('No Service' or emergency calls only)
All stored photos on the phone are automatically deleted
The phone switches its default language to Spanish
questions.explanation: Because a cellular network only allows one physical SIM card to register a given phone number at a time, the legitimate SIM is instantly deactivated, causing sudden loss of cellular signal.

questions.question: What regulatory countermeasure was mandated by India's Department of Telecommunications (DoT) to curb SIM-swap banking fraud?
options: Banning all prepaid mobile phone connections nationwide
Enforcing a mandatory 24-hour freeze on incoming and outgoing SMS services following any SIM upgrade or replacement
Requiring all phone calls to be recorded by banks
Limiting mobile phone usage to one SIM per family
questions.explanation: DoT mandated that when a SIM card is upgraded or replaced, SMS services are disabled for 24 hours, giving the legitimate owner time to notice the swap before OTPs can be intercepted.

questions.question: Why do cybersecurity experts strongly recommend replacing SMS-based two-factor authentication with authenticator apps?
options: SMS messages use too much mobile data
Authenticator apps generate time-based codes locally on the physical device and are completely unaffected by telecom SIM swapping
SMS codes are only valid for 10 seconds
Authenticator apps are sponsored by banks
questions.explanation: Time-based One-Time Password (TOTP) apps (like Google Authenticator) rely on a secret seed stored securely in the device's hardware, rendering them immune to cellular SIM swaps.

questions.question: If your phone suddenly displays 'No Service' while in an area with good coverage, what should you do immediately?
options: Wait 48 hours to see if the signal returns naturally
Contact your mobile telecom operator immediately from another device to check if a SIM replacement request was initiated
Throw away the phone and buy a new number
Reboot the phone repeatedly until the battery drains
questions.explanation: Immediate response is critical. Contacting your telecom provider allows you to halt unauthorized SIM porting or deactivate the hijacked number before criminals drain financial accounts.

title: Uber Data Breach Cover-up & Bug Bounty Extortion Quiz
description: Evaluate your understanding of breach disclosure laws, personal CISO criminal liability, bug bounty ethics, and 18 U.S.C. § 1505.

questions.question: How did Uber's security team conceal a 2016 breach involving 57 million customer and driver records?
options: By deleting all corporate emails and server backups
By paying the extortionists $100,000 disguised as an ethical 'bug bounty' reward and making them sign non-disclosure agreements
By blaming the breach on an imaginary software vendor
By claiming the stolen data belonged to a competitor
questions.explanation: Uber funneled a $100,000 extortion payment to the hackers through HackerOne's bug bounty platform, pretending it was a legitimate vulnerability reward and requiring NDAs to hide the intrusion.

questions.question: What historic legal milestone occurred in October 2022 regarding Uber's former Chief Security Officer (Joe Sullivan)?
options: He was awarded a medal by the US Federal Trade Commission
He was found guilty by a federal jury of obstruction of justice and misprision of a felony for covering up the breach from regulators
He was appointed as Director of the FBI
He was granted complete sovereign immunity by the President
questions.explanation: Joe Sullivan was convicted in federal court of obstructing an FTC proceeding and concealing a felony—marking the first time a corporate security executive faced criminal conviction for breach response actions.

questions.question: Why was Uber under heightened legal scrutiny from the FTC at the exact moment the 2016 breach took place?
options: Because Uber was applying for a banking charter
Because the FTC was actively investigating Uber for a previous 2014 data breach regarding inadequate employee access controls
Because Uber was merging with a rival ride-hailing company
Because Uber was under a criminal tax evasion audit
questions.explanation: CSO Sullivan concealed the 2016 incident specifically because Uber was already undergoing an active FTC investigation into its cybersecurity practices following a prior 2014 breach.

questions.question: How did the hackers initially obtain access to Uber's Amazon Web Services (AWS) database backups?
options: By breaking into Amazon's physical data center in Virginia
By finding unencrypted AWS credentials and access keys embedded in code stored in an Uber engineer's GitHub repository
By guessing the password on the AWS root login page
By intercepting satellite communications from Uber drivers
questions.explanation: Attackers discovered hardcoded AWS credentials stored in a private GitHub code repository accessible to Uber developers, using those keys to access S3 database backups.

questions.question: What key lesson must corporate leadership take from the Uber prosecution regarding incident response?
options: Paying bounties is the best way to handle any data extortion
Cybersecurity incident response must prioritize legal transparency and mandatory statutory disclosure over brand reputation management
Never hire a Chief Information Security Officer
All software code must be written on offline paper notebooks
questions.explanation: Corporate executives cannot use legal mechanisms or non-disclosure agreements to conceal criminal breaches from government regulators and the public without risking severe personal criminal prosecution.

title: Pegasus Zero-Click Spyware Surveillance Inquiry Quiz
description: Test your comprehension of zero-click exploits (FORCEDENTRY), constitutional privacy jurisprudence, and state surveillance limits.

questions.question: What differentiates a 'zero-click' exploit like Pegasus from conventional phishing attacks?
options: It only works on computers with external computer mice
It infects the target mobile device without requiring any interaction, clicking, or link-opening by the victim
It requires the victim to click ten different pop-up ads
It only infects devices when the user is asleep
questions.explanation: Zero-click exploits exploit background processing routines (such as image or PDF parsers in messaging apps) to execute shellcode silently without requiring the user to tap or open anything.

questions.question: What landmark nine-judge Constitution Bench judgment of the Supreme Court of India established the fundamental right to privacy?
options: Shreya Singhal v. Union of India (2015)
Justice K.S. Puttaswamy (Retd.) v. Union of India (2017)
Vishaka v. State of Rajasthan (1997)
Kesavananda Bharati v. State of Kerala (1973)
questions.explanation: In Justice K.S. Puttaswamy (2017), the Supreme Court unanimously declared the right to privacy an intrinsic part of the fundamental right to life and personal liberty under Article 21.

questions.question: In the Pegasus matter (Manohar Lal Sharma v. Union of India, 2021), what did the Supreme Court state regarding the government's claim of national security?
options: National security claims grant total immunity from any judicial oversight
The state cannot get a free pass merely by raising the phantom of national security without providing substantiated facts to the court
The court has no jurisdiction to examine cyber weapons
Only the United Nations can investigate spyware
questions.explanation: The Supreme Court ruled that while national security is paramount, the state does not get a 'free pass' merely by uttering 'national security' to evade judicial scrutiny into privacy violations.

questions.question: What specific iOS feature did Apple introduce to defend human rights defenders and journalists from targeted commercial spyware like Pegasus?
options: Apple Pay Later
Lockdown Mode, which severely restricts complex web fonts, message attachments, and shared photo albums
AirDrop Everywhere Mode
Dynamic Island notifications
questions.explanation: Apple's Lockdown Mode disables complex message attachment parsing, blocks incoming FaceTime invitations from unknown callers, and disables JIT compilation to eliminate zero-click attack surface.

questions.question: Under the three-fold test established in Puttaswamy, what three criteria must any state infringement on privacy satisfy?
options: Speed, secrecy, and cost-effectiveness
Legality (existence of a law), Legitimate Aim (necessity), and Proportionality (least intrusive means)
Presidential decree, military approval, and cabinet voting
Bipartisan consensus, UN certification, and police FIR
questions.explanation: Any state interference with privacy must satisfy legality (statutory backing), need (a legitimate state goal), and proportionality (the measure must not be excessive relative to the objective).

title: Aadhaar Biometric System Security & Privacy Quiz
description: Assess your knowledge of biometric data protections, Masked Aadhaar, the Aadhaar Act 2016, and Section 57 striking down.

questions.question: Why is biometric data (fingerprints and iris scans) considered fundamentally distinct from passwords in identity systems?
options: Biometrics expire automatically after 6 months
Biometric identifiers are immutable and permanent; once compromised or leaked, they cannot be reset, rotated, or changed like a password
Biometrics can only be processed using mainframe computers
Biometrics are public records accessible to any citizen
questions.explanation: Unlike alphanumeric passwords or tokens that can be revoked and reissued, a person's biological fingerprints and retinas are immutable attributes that cannot be reset if compromised.

questions.question: What major part of the Aadhaar Act, 2016 was struck down as unconstitutional by the 5-judge Constitution Bench in 2018?
options: Section 7, which mandated Aadhaar for government welfare subsidies
Section 57, which permitted private corporations and telecom entities to mandatorily demand Aadhaar authentication for services
The entire Aadhaar project was declared completely illegal and ordered shut down
The provision permitting children to attend school
questions.explanation: The Supreme Court struck down Section 57 of the Aadhaar Act, ruling that private commercial entities (like private banks, telecom operators, and schools) cannot compel citizens to submit Aadhaar.

questions.question: What privacy-preserving tool did UIDAI introduce to allow citizens to share their Aadhaar card while concealing the first 8 digits?
options: Laminated Aadhaar
Masked Aadhaar (which displays only the last four digits, e.g. XXXX XXXX 1234)
Aadhaar Passport
Digital Signature Token
questions.explanation: Masked Aadhaar replaces the first 8 digits of the 12-digit number with 'XXXX XXXX', obscuring the permanent identifier while retaining validity for KYC verification.

questions.question: What protective mechanism inside the official mAadhaar application allows users to prevent unauthorized biometric authentication?
options: Biometric Lock / Unlock, which temporarily freezes fingerprint and iris authentication until unlocked by the user
Deleting the Aadhaar database from the phone
Changing the fingerprint scan to an emoji
Disconnecting the SIM card permanently
questions.explanation: The Biometric Lock feature allows users to lock their biometric credentials in the CIDR. Any authentication request made while locked will be rejected until the user unlocks it.

questions.question: Under Section 29 of the Aadhaar Act, 2016, what strict prohibition is placed on core biometric information?
options: Core biometric information can be shared freely with any private marketing agency
Core biometric information shall never be shared with anyone for any reason whatsoever or used for any purpose other than authentication
Core biometric information must be published on public gazettes
Core biometric data is sold to credit rating agencies
questions.explanation: Section 29 strictly bars the sharing, publishing, or displaying of core biometric information for any reason whatsoever, creating stringent criminal liability for unauthorized disclosure.
